observations: Deployment consequence, stated honestly: until LEGION-108's listener deploys, a busy worker's delivery_failed still queues one silent catch-up (spec line 4, P11), and an alive architect sees at most three copies of one message, 5/15/45 s apart, where LEGION-103's stopgap sent none. After LEGION-108 deploys, delivery_failed means a forward that never happened and gets the bounded re-send; receipt_timeout on a live holder is logged and ignored.

The removal of LEGION-103's stopgap (MAX_ROLE_REDELIVERIES, ROLE_REDELIVERY_PERIOD_MS, the 30-minute counters, the blanket 'late receipt' ignore of delivery_failed on an alive holder, and its three tests) is deliberate per the LEGION-101 contract; no leftover text describes it as current behaviour — not a finding.

The implementer's open question (keep LEGION-103's worker-side guard — delivery_failed with a cached shim client -> log, no catch-up — as an additive branch) is the architect's call; the plan and spec route a worker's delivery_failed through resumeWorker and P11 locks one silent catch-up, which is what ships.

The cap drops the ledger entry, so a fifth exception for the same message starts a fresh chain (P14's negative control). In production a fifth exception needs a fourth copy, which the cap never sends, so a message that keeps failing yields exactly three copies; only a new original publish of a byte-identical payload restarts the count. This is the spec's own Errors row ('the ledger entry is dropped'), recorded here so nobody reads it as a loop.
